page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-4 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores via multithreading, alongside 32 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU). The x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Standard instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, whereas AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators.

Benchmark data illustrates a notable contrast between single-core and multi-threaded throughput. In single-core evaluation, the instance demonstrates solid capabilities, reaching a stress-ng single-core score of 2681.08, placing it in the top 25%, and a Geekbench single-core score of 1426.0. However, multi-core metrics reflect the physical limit of its two underlying cores, yielding a stress-ng multi-core score of 5386.56, a Geekbench multi-core score of 3257.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 6021.53. Memory throughput measures 38.56 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 28.03 GB/sec for large-block writes, landing in the middle range for memory operations.

Given its resource allocation, the n2d-highmem-4 prioritizes memory density over wide parallel processing capacity. The high memory ratio enables cost-effective execution of memory-heavy applications without incurring the cost of idle, unused compute cores. Workloads best aligned with this configuration include caching tiers, moderate relational databases, in-memory key-value stores like Redis, and memory-bound ETL batch jobs where compute parallelism is a secondary requirement.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-4 is an AMD EPYC 7B13-powered virtual machine offering 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 32 GB of RAM, and no integrated local storage or GPUs. Featuring an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, it balances memory capacity against moderate computing power. Synthetic benchmarks highlight strong single-core performance alongside lower multi-core scaling, consistent with its dual-core physical topology. Memory throughput remains balanced, handling uncached write transfers at 28.03 GB/sec. The instance delivers cost efficiency for workloads that require high RAM capacity without the overhead of purchasing surplus compute cores. It is suited for in-memory data caches, memory-intensive data pipelines, and intermediate database workloads.
